title: Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility — Hardship Discount Postings on Patient Charges
content:
**Reference card — financial-assistance discount, Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility.**

## The policy

Summit Ridge grants a financial-assistance discount on each patient charge of the deductible, coinsurance, copay or repair-patient-share type on the coverage account that the account's hardship approval covers:

- a charge posted while the approval is in force; and
- a charge already open on the approval date that was posted no more than the class's hardship lookback period, in calendar days, before it.

Each such charge receives one adjustment with the reason "hardship discount", posted against that charge.

**When the discount is posted.** A charge posted while the approval is in force receives its discount when it posts, and a charge open on the approval date receives it on that date. A discount missed at that moment is posted when the omission is found; missed discounts are worked one charge at a time, starting from the account's most recently posted patient charge.

**No approval, no discount.** An account with no hardship tier, or whose approval is no longer in force, receives no hardship discount.

**Charges never reached.** Self-pay, upgrade-difference, non-covered-with-notice and unreturned-equipment charges never receive a hardship discount, and when QMB protection applies to a charge no hardship discount is posted on it.

**Posting beyond the open amount.** For a hardship discount, and only for a hardship discount, the adjustment is posted for its full figure even where a payment has already been applied to the charge, the part above the charge's open amount staying on the account as a credit toward its other open charges. Every adjustment other than a hardship or a prompt-pay discount remains under the base rule and never stacks beyond its charge's open amount.

**Against a prompt-pay discount.** When a hardship and a prompt-pay discount could both apply to one charge, only the larger is posted, with QMB protection displacing both.

**No Medicaid record needed.** For a hardship discount, and only for a hardship discount, no Medicaid record has to be active, because the discount rests on the hardship approval alone. QMB protection itself, and every adjustment other than a hardship or a prompt-pay discount, remains under the base rule, so QMB protection applies only while the Medicaid record carrying QMB status is in status active.

## Booking the discount: `apply_hardship_discount_c60f16b6`

**Capability.** The tool books a financial-hardship discount against one patient charge on a coverage account. One call writes one hardship-discount adjustment entry dated today that points at the charge, and lowers the account's patient balance by the same amount; the patient sees the discount as a credit line under that charge on the account history.

**Invocation.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks `apply_hardship_discount_c60f16b6` with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `coverage_id` | the reference number of the coverage account (the insurance coverage record on the patient's file) that carries the charge, as returned by the coverage lookup | identifier |
| `applied_to_entry_id` | the reference number of the patient charge entry being discounted, as returned by the patient-account ledger lookup for that account | identifier |
| `amount` | the hardship discount to book on the charge, in USD | a positive figure with 2 decimal places; stored exactly as given, rounded half up to the cent |

**Return.** A text rendering of a record with `adjustment_id` (the reference of the new hardship-discount entry), `coverage_id` (the account adjusted), `applied_to_entry_id` (the charge reduced), `amount` (the discount booked, USD with 2 decimals), `posting_date` (today's date, YYYY-MM-DD), `patient_balance` (the account balance once the discount is booked, USD with 2 decimals) and `status`, the string "booked". A receipt whose status is "booked" means the discount is on the account.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A call naming account C-1, charge entry L-7 and an amount of 42.19 returns a receipt with status "booked", amount 42.19, today's posting date, and the account's patient balance lowered by 42.19.
